headline: The Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B int4 weights (15.19 GiB) consume 97% of the 15.66 GiB shared-GPU-memory budget Windows grants this iGPU (50% of 31.32 GiB system RAM), leaving 0.47 GiB. Every GB of OVMS --cache_size is RESERVED out of that same budget, evicting weights to system RAM: throughput falls 35.5 -> 18.7 -> 4.2 -> 3.3 tok/s across cache_size 1..4. The collapse is present at 0.2% pool UTILISATION, so it is caused by RESERVATION, not by cache occupancy.

the_curve.note: Two OVMS major versions, same machine, same day, same clean conditions. The runtime is not the variable.

the_mechanism.derivation: Windows grants an iGPU up to 50% of system RAM as shared GPU memory; 31.32 / 2 = 15.66 GiB. This is not user-adjustable in shipping Windows 11.
the_mechanism.kv_derivation: 2 (K,V) * 48 layers * 4 KV heads * 128 head_dim * 1 byte (u8) = 49,152 B/token
the_mechanism.why_reservation_not_occupancy: cache_size 4 measured 3.33 tok/s with OVMS's own log reporting 'cache usage: 0.2% of 4.0 GB'. An almost-empty pool produces the full collapse, so the damage is done when the pool is RESERVED out of the shared budget, not when it is filled.
the_mechanism.why_prefill_survives: Prefill degrades ~1.75x while decode degrades ~13x. Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound and re-reads evicted weights every token; prefill is compute-bound and is not.

what_this_explains_that_nothing_else_did: Model file, GPU driver, OVMS build, GPU pool size as reported by the device, power plan, thermals and contention are ALL provably unchanged or exonerated by measurement (see ruled_out). The shared-memory BUDGET is the only variable that is both invisible in every version stamp we had been comparing and sufficient to produce the observed curve.
NOT_established: Why the June 2026-06-29 baseline measured 38.58 tok/s AT cache_size 4. Under the mechanism above that result should be impossible: 15.19 + 4 = 19.19 GiB against a 15.66 GiB budget. The mechanism therefore requires that the EFFECTIVE BUDGET WAS LARGER IN JUNE. Best-supported hypothesis, NOT proven: Microsoft began a Windows 11 memory-footprint reduction programme in March 2026 with 'a more efficient memory allocator' as a named workstream, and three updates (KB5121003, KB5123304, KB5120708) installed on this machine on 2026-08-12 -- between the good baseline and the first bad measurement. NOT TESTED: rolling those updates back, or measuring the shared budget directly before/after an update. Anyone continuing this should measure the budget itself, not infer it.
ruled_out_by_measurement_this_session: OVMS version -- the identical curve reproduces on 2026.2 and 2026.3
GPU driver -- 32.0.101.8826 verified from the live device, same as the June record
Model file -- unchanged since 2026-06-10, before the good baseline
Compiled-kernel cache -- moved from C: to B:; cache_size 4 still 2.78 tok/s afterwards
Disk free space -- C: went 12.9 GB -> 35.9 GB free; no throughput change (but see disk_finding: it WAS causing a separate real defect)
AO/coder co-residency -- the AO was down for every arm here
Power plan, thermals, contention, kernel-cache recompilation, CPU fallback -- exonerated earlier the same day

disk_finding.note: A genuine, separate defect found and fixed while chasing this. It is NOT the throughput cause.
disk_finding.before: C: 12.9 GB free of 951.4 GB (1%), holding the 24 GB page file, the memory-mapped 15.19 GiB weights, and a 23.05 GiB OVMS compile cache
disk_finding.after: compile cache moved to B: (719 GB free); C: 35.9 GB free
disk_finding.what_it_actually_broke: A cold compile with a fresh cache DIED SILENTLY (process gone, empty error log) trying to write ~23 GiB into 12.9 GB. After the move, 2026.3 cold-compiled in 40 s.

operational_consequence: cache_size must be chosen against the coder's declared context window, not against throughput alone. At cache_size 1 (21,845 tokens) a measured coder session of 20,214 tokens sits at 93% and gets DESCHEDULED mid-conversation -- the coder returns nothing and the fleet reports 'produced no changes', indistinguishable from a lazy model. Shipped configuration: cache_size 2 (43,690 tokens) against a 40,960-token declared window, giving 18.7 tok/s -- 6x the broken state and comfortably inside the 600 s ACP idle breaker.
the_route_back_to_full_speed: Not recovery -- reduction. cache_size 1 still measures 35.5 tok/s on this machine TODAY. The blocker is that a coder session needs ~20.2k tokens and the 1 GB pool holds 21.8k. Roughly 5.4k of that session is an AGENTS.md loaded into every task, plus an irrelevant Azure/Foundry command registry in the ACP handshake. Cutting the session below ~18k tokens makes cache_size 1 viable and returns the machine to ~35 tok/s with no throughput compromise at all.
external_watch: Windows 11 experimental build 29648 carries 'IntelligentCarveout', a setting to explicitly reserve unified memory for graphics/AI with Custom/Recommended/High/Maximum/Don't-allow options. That is the exact control this hardware needs. Not in shipping Windows as of 2026-08-31.
not_measured: The shared-GPU-memory budget directly (before/after the August updates) -- the central claim rests on the 50%-of-RAM rule plus the fit of the curve, not on an observed budget change.
Rolling back KB5121003 / KB5123304 / KB5120708 and re-measuring -- the decisive experiment, not run.
Fractional cache_size values between 1 and 2, where the usable knee appears to lie.

MoE OFFLOAD_RATIO at LOW ratios on 2026.3 -- offloading experts reduces resident weights and is mechanistically the right lever; only ratio 30 has ever been measured here (1.71 tok/s), and that was on a box already in this state.
Whether the 14B shows the same cliff (it is roughly 9 GB and should have ~6.6 GiB of headroom, so it should not).

CORRECTION_2026-08-31.what_was_wrong: This record stated the shared-GPU budget as 15.66 GiB, DERIVED from a web article's '50% of system RAM' rule and never measured. That number is wrong.
CORRECTION_2026-08-31.how_measured: dxdiag: Display Memory 18,409 MB (Dedicated 128 MB + Shared 18,281 MB). Live confirmation: OVMS held 17.34 GiB of GPU shared usage = 96% of it.
CORRECTION_2026-08-31.note_on_the_driver_figure: OpenVINO reports GPU_DEVICE_TOTAL_MEM_SIZE = 25.17 GiB. That is the driver's advertised maximum, NOT what Windows budgets. Three numbers were in play and the published one was the only unmeasured one.
CORRECTION_2026-08-31.effect_on_the_mechanism: STRENGTHENS it. The cliff falls where weights+pool crosses 17.98 GiB (16.19 fits at 35.5 tok/s; 17.19 marginal at 18.7; 18.19 and 19.19 collapse to 4.2 and 3.3). The old 15.66 figure did NOT predict that location -- it would have put even the fast configuration over budget.
CORRECTION_2026-08-31.found_by: the LA challenging the figure, not by me re-checking it

SHORT_PROBE_WARNING.claim: Every tok/s figure in 'the_curve' above is a 128-token probe and OVERSTATES real coder throughput.
SHORT_PROBE_WARNING.evidence: cache_size 2 no-offload measured 18.7 tok/s on short probes and 11.15-12.45 tok/s under sustained realistic load (operator content in, page-sized generation out), with visible downward drift across consecutive runs.
SHORT_PROBE_WARNING.moe_offload_retracted: cs4+offload40 measured 18.5 tok/s short and 3.05 tok/s realistic; RAM 'returned' measured +6.22 GB idle and +0.87 GB under load. All offload conclusions from this session are invalid for capacity planning.
